answer: A superlinear cluster tax resists sybils. The protocol publishes a nebula of registered keys, clustered by funding paths and timing. Each new key locks a slashable bond equal to a base fee plus a surcharge that grows with its nearest cluster. An unpredictable whisper audit later re-measures those features; if the key sits closer than declared, a one-shot comet fraud proof slashes the underpaid bond. Hiding N fakes in one cluster makes the surcharge rise faster than N; spreading them still needs N funding trails and N deposits, so attacker cost scales worse than linearly with farm size.
